title: 203. Algebra, Equations & Inequalities: Solving Absolute Value Equations
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.learningObjective: Solve an absolute value equation by splitting it into two linear equations.
questions.question: Solve \(|x-3|=5\).
questions.explanation: The equation \(|x-3|=5\) means that the expression inside the absolute value is either \(5\) or \(-5\). Thus \(x-3=5\), giving \(x=8\), or \(x-3=-5\), giving \(x=-2\). Therefore the solutions are \(x=-2\) or \(x=8\).
questions.hint: Rewrite \(|x-3|=5\) as two separate linear equations: \(x-3=5\) and \(x-3=-5\).

questions.concept: Solving absolute value equations with linear expressions
questions.learningObjective: Solve an absolute value equation by considering both signs of the inside expression.
questions.question: Solve \(|2x+1|=7\).
questions.explanation: Set the expression inside the absolute value equal to \(7\) and to \(-7\). First, \(2x+1=7\) gives \(2x=6\), so \(x=3\). Second, \(2x+1=-7\) gives \(2x=-8\), so \(x=-4\). Therefore the solutions are \(x=-4\) or \(x=3\).
questions.hint: Set \(2x+1\) equal to both \(7\) and \(-7\), then solve each linear equation.

questions.concept: Isolating the absolute value before solving
questions.learningObjective: Solve an absolute value equation by first isolating the absolute value expression.
questions.question: Solve \(|x-2|+3=7\).
questions.explanation: Subtract \(3\) from both sides to isolate the absolute value: \(|x-2|=4\). Then \(x-2=4\), giving \(x=6\), or \(x-2=-4\), giving \(x=-2\). Therefore the solutions are \(x=-2\) or \(x=6\).
questions.hint: First isolate the absolute value expression, then split it into the two usual cases.

questions.concept: Absolute value equations with no solution
questions.learningObjective: Determine when an absolute value equation has no solution.
questions.question: Solve \(|x+5|=-2\).
questions.explanation: The absolute value of any real number is always nonnegative. Therefore \(|x+5|\) cannot equal \(-2\). The equation has no solution.
questions.hint: Consider whether an absolute value can ever be negative.

questions.concept: Equations with absolute values on both sides
questions.learningObjective: Solve an equation with absolute values on both sides by equating the inside expressions or their opposites.
questions.question: Solve \(|3x-1|=|x+5|\).
questions.explanation: If two absolute values are equal, then their inside expressions are equal or opposite. First, \(3x-1=x+5\) gives \(2x=6\), so \(x=3\). Second, \(3x-1=-(x+5)\) gives \(3x-1=-x-5\), so \(4x=-4\), and \(x=-1\). Therefore the solutions are \(x=-1\) or \(x=3\).
questions.hint: Set the two inside expressions equal to each other, and also set one equal to the negative of the other.

questions.concept: Absolute value equations with extraneous solutions
questions.learningObjective: Solve an absolute value equation and reject an extraneous solution.
questions.question: Solve \(|x+1|=2x-3\).
questions.explanation: Since the left side is an absolute value, it is nonnegative, so the right side must satisfy \(2x-3\ge0\), which means \(x\ge\frac{3}{2}\). Now solve the two cases. If \(x+1=2x-3\), then \(x=4\), which satisfies \(x\ge\frac{3}{2}\). If \(x+1=-(2x-3)\), then \(x+1=-2x+3\), so \(3x=2\), and \(x=\frac{2}{3}\). But \(x=\frac{2}{3}\) does not satisfy \(x\ge\frac{3}{2}\), so it is extraneous. Therefore only \(x=4\) is valid.
questions.hint: Require the right side to be nonnegative because it equals an absolute value, then check each candidate.

questions.concept: Absolute value equations requiring domain checking
questions.learningObjective: Solve an absolute value equation by checking candidates against a nonnegative condition.
questions.question: Solve \(|2x-5|=x+1\).
questions.explanation: The right side equals an absolute value, so it must be nonnegative: \(x+1\ge0\), or \(x\ge-1\). Solve the two cases. If \(2x-5=x+1\), then \(x=6\), which satisfies \(x\ge-1\). If \(2x-5=-(x+1)\), then \(2x-5=-x-1\), so \(3x=4\), and \(x=\frac{4}{3}\), which also satisfies \(x\ge-1\). Therefore the solutions are \(x=\frac{4}{3}\) or \(x=6\).
questions.hint: Impose the condition \(x+1\ge0\), then solve both linear cases and check the condition.

questions.concept: Solving absolute value equations with two absolute value expressions
questions.learningObjective: Solve an equation of the form \(|ax+b|=|cx+d|\).
questions.question: Solve \(|x-4|=|2x+1|\).
questions.explanation: For two absolute values to be equal, the inside expressions are equal or opposite. First, \(x-4=2x+1\) gives \(-5=x\), so \(x=-5\). Second, \(x-4=-(2x+1)\) gives \(x-4=-2x-1\), so \(3x=3\), and \(x=1\). Therefore the solutions are \(x=-5\) or \(x=1\).
questions.hint: Set the two inside expressions equal, and also set one equal to the negative of the other.

questions.concept: Absolute value equations with two absolute value terms and a constant
questions.question: Solve \(|x-3|+|x+1|=6\).
questions.explanation: The critical points are \(x=-1\) and \(x=3\). Test the intervals. If \(x<-1\), then \(|x-3|=-(x-3)\) and \(|x+1|=-(x+1)\), so \(-(x-3)-(x+1)=6\), which simplifies to \(-2x+2=6\), giving \(x=-2\). This satisfies \(x<-1\). If \(-1\le x<3\), then \(|x-3|=-(x-3)\) and \(|x+1|=x+1\), so \(-(x-3)+(x+1)=4\), which is not equal to \(6\). If \(x\ge3\), then \(|x-3|=x-3\) and \(|x+1|=x+1\), so \((x-3)+(x+1)=6\), which simplifies to \(2x-2=6\), giving \(x=4\). This satisfies \(x\ge3\). Therefore the solutions are \(x=-2\) or \(x=4\).
questions.hint: Split the number line at \(x=-1\) and \(x=3\), then solve the equation on each interval.

questions.concept: Parameter conditions for absolute value equations
questions.learningObjective: Determine a parameter value that makes an absolute value equation have exactly one solution.
questions.question: For what value of \(k\) does the equation \(|3x-2|=k-1\) have exactly one solution?
questions.explanation: An equation of the form \(|3x-2|=c\) has exactly one solution when \(c=0\), because then \(3x-2=0\) gives the single solution \(x=\frac{2}{3}\). Thus we need \(k-1=0\), so \(k=1\). If \(k=-1\), then \(k-1=-2\), and the equation \(|3x-2|=-2\) has no solution.
questions.hint: Think about how many solutions \(|u|=c\) has when \(c>0\), \(c=0\), and \(c<0\).
